decisions.reason: The margin analysis builds on the firm's core market-data assets, has its own web page as a visible commitment, and fits the announced platform strategy, so management would attribute any slow uptake to a normal ramp-up period.
The gas tariff comparison sits close to the established offer, costs little to maintain on existing databases, and is publicly presented, which makes withdrawing it after one year unlikely.
The electricity tariff calculator is a core-adjacent tool with its own page and sunk development costs, and it strengthens the central platform, so management persists with it.

This multi-model line was a substantial investment, but because it is only mentioned on the website rather than featured, it could be merged or consolidated; escalation of commitment still favors keeping it.
The area definition tool supports the firm's other location-based products and the platform, and it is visibly presented, so it is likely retained.
The site-specific comparison line overlaps with other tariff tools and has only modest web visibility, but the investment in several models and the fit with the core business argue for keeping it.
